speaker: M. S. Agranovich
title: Pseudodifferential and singular integral operators
summary: The first Agranovich lecture introduces homogeneous symbols, spherical harmonic kernels, rough-symbol boundedness and the first rules of symbolic calculus. It is primarily an exposition of the already published 1965 theory, not a preview whose first publication was necessarily after the seminar. Several handwritten slips in the boundedness argument are separated from transcription mistakes. The lecture ends in the upper part of P000128, before Gelfand's integral-geometry heading.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Integral geometry on affine k-planes
summary: The lecture develops differential forms attached to the affine \(k\)-plane transform: a generalized determinant, a closedness criterion for the range, and inversion by integrating over cycles. The close publication is \citet{gelfand1967planes}, with Graev and Shapiro. Its hypotheses and quantifiers correct two potentially serious overstatements in the notebook. P000128 starts this record after Agranovich; P000132 ends it before Karpelevich.

speaker: F. I. Karpelevich
title: Klein on the spinning top
summary: A short exposition of Klein's Princeton lectures describes rotations by fractional linear transformations and reduces a top problem to an elliptic integral. The lecture crosses the page boundary: its final quadrature is at the top of P000133, before the dated Agranovich continuation. The two cyclic-momentum formulas contain a factor-of-two slip already present in the handwriting.

speaker: M. S. Agranovich
title: Symbolic calculus, elliptic operators and index
summary: The continuation assembles the local calculus on a manifold and derives the Fredholm and regularity theorems from a parametrix. It then states Seeley's special degree formula for the index and ends with Hörmander's oscillatory characterization. The exact Seeley theorem, including its equivalence with vanishing of lower-rank indices, was checked in the full paper's Russian translation; the 1965 English original is the historical publication.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Borel and Tits: algebraic and reductive groups
summary: This is an introductory report on Borel and Tits, not an announcement of a new classification. It passes from schemes and Chevalley's structure theorem to radicals, tori and root systems. Connectedness and the ground field are repeatedly tacit. The example calling an algebraic torus an abelian variety is incompatible with the standard algebraic-group meaning of torus and is retained as a source-level error.

speaker: V. A. Borovikov; comment by I. M. Gelfand
title: Boundary integrals and area
summary: After the dated March heading, Borovikov states a double boundary cosine integral for area. Gelfand follows with a very compressed slice-area/volume formula. The former is valid with convexity and consistent inward chord-angle conventions; it has no missing distance denominator. The latter is false for a single slicing direction and remains uncertain as a historical assertion because an angular average may have been omitted.

speaker: V. B. Lidskii
title: Zeta function of all zeros of an exponential-type entire function
summary: This compact announcement has an unusually exact later match: Lidskii and Sadovnichii's 1967 paper, especially Lemmas 2--3. The entire continuation concerns a branch-dependent sum over all nonzero zeros, with complete sectorial asymptotics. The comparison with the ordinary zeta function refers to the difference between all signed sine zeros and only the positive half.

speaker: S. G. Gindikin
title: Generalized parabolic equations and cone-valued ellipticity
summary: Gindikin's announcement precedes Minlos in the physical notebook, although the catalogue numbers it 89. The 1967 multidimensional-time paper identifies both the hyperbolic replacement of the time derivative and the \(V\)-elliptic mapping. A reinspection corrects the transcription's pseudo-operator to hyperbolic operator. The random-walk/heat sentence before the boxed Minlos heading is recorded here with attribution uncertainty.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Ising lattice gas and thermodynamic limit
summary: The boxed Minlos heading introduces a lattice-gas configuration sum and the limit of its logarithm per volume. This is a brief substantive reminder, not a content-free heading, but no low-temperature contour theorem or phase-transition statement is actually recorded. It recurs to the elementary material indexed as 1964-3.1 and 1964-3.2.
